# Running delulu-smash on Windows

Notes from getting `uv run reflex run` going on Windows (Nov 2026, branch `os-windows`). The rules the code
follows to stay cross platform are in `spec/services/ui/README.md` ("Platforms: Omarchy (Arch Linux) and
Windows"); this file is the how-to and what was seen.

## Branch strategy: one branch, two computers

The Windows work is done on one branch, `os-windows`, from two computers. The Linux machine writes the
changes and pushes them; the work Windows laptop only pulls (it commits locally and never pushes), so its
own edits stay on it. Taking the Linux machine's changes on the laptop:

```bash
git add <files> && git commit -m "local: ..."   # commit first: pull refuses to overwrite uncommitted edits
git pull --rebase                                # the laptop's commits go on top of what came in
git log --stat ORIG_HEAD..HEAD                   # what arrived, with each commit's why
```

- The full guide (which machine you are on, the laptop's constraints, how to resolve each kind of conflict,
  the context of the changes so far) is `.agents/instructions/os_windows.md`, written for the AI on either
  machine.
- A side branch (eg `os-windows-updates`) wouldn't avoid conflicts, only delay them to its merge.
- `uv.lock`: don't merge it by hand; take the pulled one, then run `uv lock` again.
- **No Git LFS on this branch, and why**: the Windows computer can't fetch LFS files (a pull left 132-byte
  placeholders for the parquet tables and the app's fonts, so the data and icons were missing). So on
  `os-windows` they are plain git files (`04e32c4`; 2.6 MB in all, the commit hook exempts their folders).
  The first pull after that commit replaces the placeholders with the real files; no `git lfs pull`.
- When the Windows work is done, `os-windows` is merged into `main` (no pull request: `.agents/agents.md`).

| Date | Where | What | Result |

| 2026-11-19 | Omarchy's Windows VM, MSYS2 UCRT64 shell, branch `os-windows` at `32168a0` | `uv run reflex run` in `services/ui` | compiled, "App running at http://localhost:3000/", backend on `http://127.0.0.1:8000` |

Not checked on Windows yet: the page itself (chat, Results, SmashDb, VODs, Python cells, Config), and
`.install.sh` from start to end.

## Install once

- **Git for Windows**: brings Git Bash. No git-lfs needed: the data files and fonts are plain git files.
- **uv**, from PowerShell or Git Bash, then reopen the shell:

  ```bash
  powershell -ExecutionPolicy ByPass -c "irm https://astral.sh/uv/install.ps1 | iex"
  ```

Nothing else: `uv` fetches Python and the packages, and Reflex fetches Bun (see below) on its first run.
No font either: the app's mono font and its icons come with the repo (`services/ui/assets/nerd_fonts/`).

## Start the app

In Git Bash (bash commands, the same as on Linux):

```bash
git clone https://github.com/delulu-smash/delulu-smash.git
cd delulu-smash
git switch os-windows
bash .install.sh          # uv sync and the commit hook; Ctrl+D at the key prompt skips it
cd services/ui
uv run reflex run         # then open http://localhost:3000 in a browser on the same machine
```

- Later runs need only the last two lines (and `git pull` for new changes).
- The first run is slow: Reflex downloads Bun and the page's JavaScript packages, then compiles.
- Git Bash is only the shell: the Python that runs is Windows' own, so the Unix-only parts stay unavailable.

## Run it in the background, with an icon and Ctrl+Alt+J

Once the app starts by hand (above), set it up like on Omarchy, in Git Bash at the repo root:

```bash
uv run ds ui install
```

```
Created scheduled task "delulu-smash" (runs at logon, restarts on failure)
Created shortcut: C:\Users\<you>\Desktop\delulu-smash.lnk   (hotkey CTRL+ALT+J)
Created shortcut: C:\Users\<you>\AppData\Roaming\Microsoft\Windows\Start Menu\Programs\delulu-smash.lnk
Command run: schtasks /Run /TN delulu-smash
Waiting for delulu-smash to answer (up to about a minute)...
delulu-smash is up: http://localhost:3000
```

- **What it made**: a Task Scheduler task (`taskschd.msc`, "delulu-smash") that runs `ds ui run` at your
  logon with the repo venv's `pythonw.exe`, so no console window; it restarts the server up to 3 times if it
  crashes. Per user, only while logged on: no admin needed. Its log, pid file, task XML and icon are in
  `%LOCALAPPDATA%\delulu-smash\`.
- **The icon / Ctrl+Alt+J** run `.os/scripts/keybindings/delulu-smash.py`, the same launcher as SUPER+SHIFT+J:
  if the server is down, a toast says it is starting; then an Edge app window opens on the page, or the
  open one comes to the front.
- **Commands** (as on Omarchy): `ds ui status`, `ds ui restart`, `ds ui logs -f` (instead of journalctl),
  `ds ui uninstall` (removes the task and the icons).
- **If Windows refuses the task** (eg a work machine's policy), `install` says so and puts a "delulu-smash
  server" shortcut in the Startup folder instead: it starts at logon, but isn't restarted after a crash.
- **Running by hand** (`uv run reflex run`) still works; stop the background one first (`ds ui uninstall`, or
  end it in Task Scheduler), as both use ports 3000 and 8000.
- Ctrl+Alt+J, not SUPER+SHIFT+J: a shortcut's own hotkey must be Ctrl+Alt+<key> on Windows.

## The "allow Bun" firewall question

On the first run Windows asks "Do you want to allow public and private networks to access this app?" for
**Bun**. Bun is the JavaScript runtime Reflex installs and uses to build and serve the page (the server on
port 3000). It opens a network port, so Windows Firewall asks.

- **Cancel** is enough to use the app in a browser on the same machine (`localhost` is never blocked).
- **Allow** only when another machine should open the page (eg the Omarchy host opening the VM's page).

## In the Omarchy Windows VM

- `~/Windows` on Omarchy is the folder shared with the VM: inside Windows it is the "Shared" folder on the
  desktop, `\\host.lan\Data` (`//host.lan/Data` in Git Bash). Good for passing a script or a traceback across.
- Clone the repo inside the VM (eg the home folder), not into the shared folder: a network share is slow for
  the thousands of small files Reflex writes, and symlinks can fail there.
- Open a shared file from Git Bash: `notepad //host.lan/Data/<file>`.

## The setup script used in the VM

Saved on Omarchy as `~/Windows/delulu-smash-setup.sh` (the shared folder, so not in the repo). In the VM:
`bash //host.lan/Data/delulu-smash-setup.sh`, or open it with `notepad` and paste a line at a time.

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# AUTO-GENERATED by Claude Code
# Purpose: first run of delulu-smash in the Windows VM (Git Bash): clone the os-windows
#          branch, install, start the app. Needs Git for Windows and uv installed first.
# Usage: in Git Bash:   bash //host.lan/Data/delulu-smash-setup.sh
#        or open this file in Notepad and paste the lines one at a time.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
set -e

# uv, if it isn't installed yet (then close and reopen Git Bash):
#   powershell -ExecutionPolicy ByPass -c "irm https://astral.sh/uv/install.ps1 | iex"

cd ~
[ -d delulu-smash ] || git clone https://github.com/delulu-smash/delulu-smash.git
cd delulu-smash
git switch os-windows
git pull

# installs packages and pulls the data; press Ctrl+D at the key prompt to skip it
bash .install.sh || echo "install stopped early: see the message above"

# the app: open http://localhost:3000 in the VM's browser once it says it is running
cd services/ui
uv run reflex run
```

## What to expect

- **No keys stored**: the app runs without the AI, and its controls are not on the page
  (`spec/services/ui/README.md`, "The app works without the AI"). A missing start.gg token shows as an error
  where it is used, not a crash.
- **Terminal panel**: one line, "The Terminal needs a Unix shell (Linux, macOS, WSL): it isn't available on
  Windows yet."
- **Warnings in the console** (harmless, the same on Linux): the `SitemapPlugin` notice, and "Your version of
  reflex is out of date".
- **Other gaps** (each fails in its own place): `from_url`'s browser fallback, the Spend view's days in UTC,
  no memory numbers in the debug panel's System tab, and `os sync` (Omarchy only; run `ds ui install` once instead).
  The table is in the spec.

## If something fails

Copy the traceback from the console (into the shared folder if copy and paste doesn't cross) and fix it on
the `os-windows` branch; keep `tests/test_cross_platform.py` passing, and add a row to the table at the top
for what was run.
